The House met at eleven of the clock, Mr. Chairman in the Chair. 
HOMAGE TO MARTYRS OF THE QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Honourable Members, today, the 9th August is a very 
historic and momentous day in the annals of our nation. It was on this day in 
1942, that Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, gave a call to the 
British Government to 'QUIT INDIA'. The whole nation responded to the 
call of Gandhiji and participated in the movement with single-minded 
commitment and dedication, which culminated in our achieving 
Independence, five years later. 
Today is a day of thanks giving and dedication, a day of remembrance and 
reverence. We pay our humble and respectful homage to all those martyrs 
who gave their lives and to all those who underwent untold sufferings for the 
cause of Independence. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of martyrs and freedom-fighters. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
REFERENCE TO THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE DROPPING OF 
ATOMIC BOMBS ON HIROSHIMA AND NAGASAKI 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Honourable Members, I refer to the nuclear 
catastrophe that struck the mankind fifty-six years ago. The dreaded 'ATOM 
BOMB' was dropped on the two Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki 
on the 6th and 9th August, 1945 killing over two lakh innocent civilians and 
leaving the survivors scarred for life. The trail of suffering, misery and 
destruction was so immense that the dead became the envy of the living. 
We urge that Hiroshima and Nagasaki must never be repeated and such 
weapons of mass destruction must never be used again under any 
circumstances.

mark of respect to the memory of the victims of the atom bomb.

Open Storage of wheat at Najafgarh and Narela in Delhi 
*261. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR BIRLA: Will the Minister of 
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that FCI godo wns are packed with foodgrains 
meant for export while huge stocks of wheat purchased by the Corporation 
for release through PDS has been lyi ng in open at the grain markets at 
Najafgarh and Narela in Delhi for want of storage facilities; 
(b) if so, what is estimated loss likely to be suffered by FCI as a result 
thereof; and 
(c) what measures have been taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHANTA KUMAR): (a) to (c) A statement is laid 
on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) No, Sir. The wheat procured by FCI is not lying in the open at 
Najafgarh and Narela mandis. All the wheat stocks procured by FCI 
from the said mandis have already been shifted to storage complexes. 
It may also be mentioned that there is no distinction between stocks meant 
for export and stocks meant for distribution under PDS or other schemes. 
The demand for export of foodgrains is limited, though FCI has huge stocks 
available with it which are far in exces s of the buffer stocking norms. The 
foodgrains are stored in FCI godowns in a scientific manner. 
(b) and (c) Do not arise in view of the reply to part (a) above.

Statement 
(a) to (d) Government is aware of the problems of the workers engaged in 
the unorganised sector, which constitutes almost 92% of the workforce in the 
country. Majority of these worker s are engaged in agriculture where 
employment is of seasonal nature. Some of the major steps taken by the 
Government for providing employment opportunities and improving the 
conditions of the workers in the unorganised sector arc as follows:—  
(i) Special programmes for eradication of poverty and generation of 
employment are being implemented throughout the country. The 
major poverty alleviation programmes, which provide employment 
in the rural areas are—Swarna Jayati Gram Swarozgar Yojana, 
Jawahar Gram Samriddhi Yojana, Employment Assurance Scheme 
and Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana. In the urban areas, Swarna 
Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yajana (SJSRY) is in operation since 1.12.97 
for providing gainful employment to the poor. Prime Minister's 
Rozgar Yojana is being implemented to provide employment 
opportunities to educated unemployed youth in both rural and urban 
areas. 
(ii) Ninth Plan has accorded priority to agriculture and rural development 
with a view to generating adequate productive employment and 
eradication of poverty. The Plan ha s focused on sectors, sub-sectors 
and technologies which arc labour in tensive, in regions characterized 
by higher rates of unemployment and underemployment. According to 
NSSO estimates, total employment in the country has risen from 374 
million in 1993-94 to 397 million in 1999-2000 (based on Usual Principal 
and Subsidiary Status). 
(iii) Task Force under Chairmanship of Dr. M.S. Ahluwalia was set up by 
the Planning Commission to suggest strategies for employment 
generation for achieving the target of providing employment 
opportunities to one crore people per year on an average over the  
next  10 years.  In the report, which has

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHRIRAM 
CHAUHAN): (a) to (d) Iraq has recently  rejected four consignments of 
wheat shipped by there private partie s from India insisting that the cargo 
should be totally free from inorganic matter, such as, sand silica, dust and 
asphalt, and also live insects. As per the International CODES standards, 
foreign matter in the grain is permissible upto 2% out of which 1.5% consists 
of organic matter, such as, chaff, weed  seeds, other edible and non-edible 
grains, etc. and the balance (0.5%) inor ganic foreign matter, such as, stones, 
dust, etc. Quality specifications prescrib ed in the Iraqi contract provided for 
the presence of foreign matter upto 2%. The inspection agency agreed by the 
Grain Board of Iraq had inspected the car go prior to shipment and declared 
the wheat consignments fit for human consumption and conforming to the 
quality specifications of the Iraqi or der. However, on arrival of the 
consignments at Iraqi ports, the Grain Board of Iraq insisted on 'nil' tolerance 
for inorgainc foreign matter. The Indian delegation that visited Iraq in May, 
2001 was informed by Iraqi authoritie s that, according to their definition, 
they do not count sand particles under foreign matter. In other works, 
inorganic matter, which is a part and parcel of foreign matter, like sand, 
stones, pebbles, clay particles, etc., are not accepted under this category. The 
explanation given by them was that only organic foreign matter (like chaff, 
glumes, weed seeds and other edible and inedible grains) are taken under this 
category. The exporters did not know this position. They presumed that, as in 
the CODES Standards, the 2% foreign matter would include upto 0.5% in-
orgainc matter. The delegation was further informed that the Iraqi flour mills 
were not having adequate facilities for separation of non-organic matter 
because of the problem of spare parts required for maintenance of such 
machines owing to UN sanctions.  The delegation was told that the Iraqi 
authorities had

Statement  
Measures/steps taken by FCI/CWC for safe storage of foodgrains 
To ensure safe storage of foodgrains and avoid any damage (excepting due 
to unforeseen/natural calamities), the following steps are taken by FCI/CWC. 
(i) Foodgrains with moisture content within the safe storage limit as per 
uniform specification are procured/accepted for storage. 
(ii) Stocks are accepted for storage in storage worthy constructed g6downs 
or on pucca plinths duly covered by polythene covers properly lashed to 
prevent ballooning due to high velocity wind. The constructed godowns 
have high plinths to prevent floodings. 
54 

[9 August, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
 
(iii) Stocks arc also accepted on suitable dunnage such as wooden crates or 
bamboo mats sandwiched with polythene film to avoid absorption of 
floor seepage. 
(iv) Stocks are properly stacked and periodically inspected very fortnight to 
check development of insect infestation, if any. 
(v) The stocks are prophylactically treated with Daltamethrin, Malathion, 
DDVP for prevention of insect infestation. 
(vi) In case of detection of insect infestation immediate curative action by 
way of fumigation with suitable fumigant is undertaken. 
(vii) The stocks are issued on "first-in-first-out" basis so as to avoid damage 
to stocks due to prolonged storage.

Supply of Foodgrains to Targeted Groups 
1979. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the steps taken by Government to ensure that the supplies from 
the Public Distribution Syst em reach the targeted groups including the people 
living below poverty line and those under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana families; 
(b) whether those living in the drought-hit areas in the country would also 
be covered by the scheme of PDS; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN -THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHRIRAM 
CHAUHAN): (a) Public Distribution System (PDS) is operated under the joint 
responsibility of Central and the State Governments. The Central Government 
has taken the responsibility for procurement, storage, transportation and bulk 
allocation at subsidised prices of certain essential items, viz., rice, wheat, sugar, 
imported edible oils and kerosene. The responsibility of distribution to the 
consumer through the network of FPSs rests with the State Government. The 
Government of India has advised the State Governments to substantially involve 
the Gram Panchayats in the supervision and monitoring of the Public Distribution 
System, especially at the fair price shop level, as a measure of social audit. The 
involvement of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the implementation of the PDS at the 
grass root level will make the system transparent and accountable and thereby 
help in ensuring that the supplies from PDS reach the targeted groups including 
people living below poverty line and the poorest of poor "Antyodaya" families. 
The guidelines issued by the Government of India for Antyodaya Anna Yojana 
provide that the allocation of foodgrains to the States will be linked to the 
receipt of utilisation certificates fro m them to the effect that the f oodgrains 
already allocated have actually reached the Antyodaya families.

areas in the country.

subsistence from his/her own source of income or through financial support

entitlement cards to the beneficiarie s which entitles them to receive the 
foodgrains.

expenditure of 75% of available funds, as required in terms of the guidelines 
for the scheme.

Steps taken by the Government to promote IT Hardware Sector 
1. Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG) has been rationalised 
and extended uniformly to all sectors without any threshold limit on payment 
of 5% duty. 
2. Approvals for all foreign direct investment proposals relating to the 
Information Technology sector, with the exception of Business-to-consumer 
(B2C) e-commerce are under the automatic route.

implemented under the aegis of the Ministry of Information 
Technology through a single window mechanism of the Inter- 
Ministerial Standing Committee (IMSC).

electronics hardware units under EOU/EPZ^EHTP schemes. Broadbanding 
is permitted in the DTA sales of Hardware units for items covered in the 
Letter of Permission.

for electronic units under Export-O riented schemes (EOU/EPZ/STP/EHTP) 
have been enhanced. These shall stand depreciated to overall limit of 90% 
over a period of 3 years instead of around 5 year earlier.

manufacturing and trading for export purposes.

to 33% under Advance Licensing Scheme.

Customs duty surcharge @10% has been abolished on all imports, in general 
but Special Additional Duty (SAD) @4% continues on all imports, except 
specific exemptions. In the 2000-2001 Budget, Customs duty on Computers 
and Peripherals had been reduced from 20% to 15% and continues to be

monitors also continues   at   0%.   In   the   2001>02   Budget,   Customs

Prevention of Harassment of Women 
2071. DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the salient features of the guidelin es laid down by the Supreme Court 
in the case of Visakha and others Vs. the State of Rajasthan for prevention of 
sexual harassment of women at work place; 
(b) whether these have been included in the conduct rules of Government 
employees; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL 
AND TRAINING OF THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): 
(a) A Statement is annexed (See below). 
(b) the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 have been amended 
inserting a new rule relating to prohibition of sexual harassment of working 
women. 
(c) Does not arise. 
Statement 
Salient features of the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in 
the  case  of Visakha  and  others   Vs.   the  State  of Rajasthan for 
prevention of sexual harassment of women at work place. 
In the case of Visakha and others Vs. State of Rajasthan and others (JT 
1997(7) SC 384) the Supreme Court has laid down as follows:—  
HAVING REGARD to the definition of 'human rights* in Section 2(d) of 
the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, TAKING NOTE of the fact that 
the present civil and penal laws in India do not adequately provide for 
specific protection of women from sexual harassment in work places and that 
enactment of such legislation will take considerable time. 
It is necessary and expedient for employers in work places as 
162 

[9 August, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
well as other responsible persons or institutions to observe certain guidelines 
to ensure the prevention of sexual harassment of women. 
1. Duty of the Employer or other re sponsible persons in work places and 
other institutions: 
It shall be the duty of the employer or other responsible persons in work 
places or other institutions to prevent or deter the commission of acts of 
sexual harassment and to provide the procedures for the resolution, settlement 
or prosecution of acts of sexual harassment by taking all steps required. 
2. Definition: 
For this purpose, sexual harassmen t includes such unwelcome sexually 
determined behaviour (whether directly or by implication) as: 
(a) Physical contact and advances; 
(b) a demand or request for sexual favours; 
(c) sexual coloured remarks; 
(d) showing pornography; 
(e) any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual 
nature. 
Where any of these acts is committed in circumstances where-under the 
victim of such conduct has a reasonable  apprehension that in relation to the 
victim's employment or work whether she is drawing salary, or honorarium or 
voluntary, whether in government, public or private enterprise such conduct 
can be humiliating and may constitute a health and safety problem. It is 
discriminatory for instance when the woman has reasonable grounds to 
believe that her objection would disadvantage her in connection with her 
employment or work including recruiting or promotion or when it creates a 
hostile work environment. Adverse consequences might be visited if the 
victim does not consent to the conduct in question or raises any objection 
thereto. 
163 

RAJYA SABHA [9 August, 2001] 
 
3. Preventive Steps:  
All employers or persons in charge of work place whether in public or 
private sector should take appropriat e steps to prevent sexual harassment. 
Without prejudice to the generality of this obligation they should take the 
following steps: 
(a) Express prohibition of sexual harassment as defined above at the work 
place should be notified, publishe d and circulated in appropriate 
ways. 
(b) The Rulcs^Rcgulations of Government and Public Sector bodies 
relating to conduct and discipline should include rules/ regulations 
prohibting sexual harassment and provide for appropriate penalties in 
such iulcs against the offender. 
(c) As regards private employers steps should be taken to include the 
aforesaid prohibitions in the standing orders under the Industrial 
Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946. 
(d) Appropriate work conditions should be provided in respect of work, 
leisure, health and hygiene to further ensure that there is no hostile 
environment towards women at wo rk places and no employee woman 
should have reasonable grounds to believe that she is disadvantaged in 
connection with her employment. 
4. Criminal proceedings:  
Where such conduct amounts to a specific offence under the Indian Penal 
Code or under any other law, the employer shall initiate appropriate action in 
accordance with law by making a complaint with the appropriate authority. 
In particular, it should ensure that vi ctims, or witnesses are not victimized 
or discriminated against while dealing with complaints of sexual harassment. 
The victims of sexual harassment should have the option to seek transfer of 
the perpetrator or their own transfer. 
5. Disciplinary Action:  
Where such conduct amounts to misconduct in employment as defined by 
the relevant service rules, appropriate disciplinary action should be 
initiated by the employer in accordance with those rules. 
164 

[9 August, 2001] RAJYA SABHA     
6. Complaint Mechanism:  
Whether or not such conduct constitutes an offence under law or a breach 
of the service rules, an appropriate complaint mechanism should be created 
in the employer's organization for redress of the complaint made by victim. 
Such complaint mechanism should ensure time bound treatment of 
complaints. 
7. Complaints Committee : 
The complaint mechanism, referred to in (6) above, should be adequate to 
provide, where necessary, a Complaints  Committee^ a speci al counselor or 
other support service, including the maintenance of confidentiality. 
The Complaints Committee should be headed by a woman and not less 
than half of its member should be women. Further, to prevent the possibility 
of any undue pressure or influence from senior levels, such Complaints 
Committee should involve a third party, either NGO or other body who is 
familiar with the issue of sexual harassment. 
The Complaints Committee must make an annual report to the 
Government department concerned of the complaints and action taken by 
them. 
The employers and person in charge will also report on the compliance 
with the aforesaid guidelines including on the reports of the Complaints 
Committee to the Government department. 
8. Worker's Initiative:  
Employees should be allowed to raise issues of sexual harassment at 
workers' meeting and in other appropriate forum and it should be affirmatively 
discussed in Employer-Employee Meetings. 
9. Awareness: 
Awareness of the rights of female employees in this regard should be 
created in particular by prominently notifying the guidelines (and appropriate 
legislation when enacted on the subject) in a suitable manner. 
165 

RAJYA SABHA [9 August, 2001) 
10. Third Party Harassment: 
Where sexual harassment occurs as a result of an act or omission by any 
third party or outsider, the employer and person in charge will take all steps 
necessary and reasonable to assist the affected person in terms of support and 
preventive action. 
11. The CentrakState Governments are requested to consider 
adopting suitable measures including legislation to ensure that the 
guidelines laid down by this order are also observed by the employers 
in Private Sector. 
12. These guidelines will not prejudice any rights available under 
the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

CHAPTER-III 
RECRUITMENT 
"Appointing Authorities": 
Appointment to a post under the Institute shall be made: 
(i) In the case of temporary and permanent posts of Grades I & II, by 
the Administrative Officer; 
(ii) In the case of temporary and perm anent posts in Grades III to VIII, 
by the Director; 
(iii) In the case of a temporary po st in Grades IX and X-l, by the 
Director; 
(iv) In the case of permanent posts in Grades IX and X-l, and temporary 
and permanent posts in the Grad es above X-l, by the Executive 
Council. 
Methods of Recruitment 
(1) Recruitment to a post under the Institute may be made, 
(i) by promotion; or 
(ii) by direct recruitment; or (iii) by 
transfer or deputation. 
(2) The Sanctioning Authority sh all in each case determine the 
methods by which a vacancy shall be filled.

[9 August, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Recruitment by Promotion 
(1) Appointment to a post in any grade by promotion shall be 
made, whether in a substantive or officiating capacity—  
(i) from amongst employees serving in posts in the next lower grade; 
or 
(ii) from amongst employees of outstanding ability and merit serving 
in the next lower grade but one. 
(2) Every appointment by promotion shall be by selection on the 
basis of merit, with regard to seniority and on the recommendations 
of a Selection Committee; provided that every appointment to Grade 
VI and above shall be made solely on the basis of merit. 
Direct Recruitment 
Appointment to any post by direct recruitment for all the Grades may he 
made on the recommendations of a Selection Committee—  
(i) in Grades I to IV from agmonst candidates recommended by the 
Employment Exchange on requisition; or 
(ii) from amongst candidates registered for a period not exceeding one 
year in the register, to be maintained by the Institute for the 
purpose; or 
(iii) from amongst candidates applying in response to any 
advertisement. 
Appointment by Transfer or Deputation 
Appointment by transfer or deputatio n may be made to any post with the 
approval of the Selection Committee on such terms and conditions as the 
Sanctioning Authority may deem proper. 
Qualifications 
The qualifications for appointment to any post shall be such as may be 
determined by the Sanctioning Authority.

(i) he produces at his own cost a certificate of health in the form

the Director in this behalf; and 
(ii) the Appointing Authority is satisfied that he possesses good 
character and antecedents.

(SHRLARUN SHOURIE): (a) and (b) The National Commission on

comparative position of each district in relation to these indicators. However,

(c) Though the Family Welfare Programme is being implemented all over

Population Policy 2000 lays down the following 14 National Socio-
Demographic Goals to be achieved by 2010: 
(1) Address the unmet needs for basic reproductive and child 
health services, supplies and infrastructure. 
(2) Make school education up to age 14 free and compulsory, and reduce 
drop outs at primary and secondary school levels to below 20 per cent for 
both boys and girjs. 
(3) Reduce infant mortality rate to below 30 per 1000 live births. 
(4) Reduce maternal mortality ratio to below 100 per 100,000 live births. 
(5) Achieve universal imm unization of children against all vaccine 
preventable diseases. 
(6) Promote delayed marriage for girl s, not earlier th an age 18 and 
preferably after 20 years of age. 
(7) Achieve 80 per cent institutional deliveries arfd 100 per cent deliveries 
by trained persons. 
(8) Achieve universal access to informa tion/counselling and services for 
fertility regulation and contraception with a wide basket of choices.

(9) Achieve 100 per cent registration of births, deaths marriages 
and pregnancies. 
(10) Contain the spread of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), 
and promote greater integration between the management of reproductive 
tract infections (RTI) and sexually transmitted infections (STI) and the 
National AIDS Control Organisation. 
(11) Prevent and control communicable diseases. 
(12) Integrate Indian Systems of Medicine (ISM) in the provision of 
reproductive and child health services, and in reaching out to households. 
(13) Promote vigorously the small family norm to achieve replacement 
levels of TFR. 
(14) Bring about convergence in implemen tation of related social sector 
program so that family welfare becomes a people centred programme.

regarding alleviation of poverty in the world, with the objective of reducing 
the number of those earning less than a dollar a day, by 50 per cent by the 
year 2015 was made; and

179

Millennium Declaration at the UN Millennium Summit held between 6-8

people, whose income is less than one US dollar a day, by the year 2015.

The Planning Commission destimates the incidence of poverty from the 
large sample survey on consumer expenditure conducted by the National 
Sample Survey Organization (NSSO) at an interval of approximately five 
years, based on the methodology contained in the Report of the Expert Group

line are estimated from the state-specific poverty lines and state-specific 
consumption distribution obtained from the large sample surveys on 
consumer expenditure conducted by the NSSO. The latest available estimate 
of poverty based on the 55th Round of the consumer expenditure data of the 
NSSO, covering the period July, 1999 to June, 2000 shows that 26.1% of the 
population lived below the poverty line in the country during 1999-2000. 
State-wise estimates of poverty for the year 1999-2000 are given in 
Statement-I (See below). 
The Ninth Five Year Plan projected th e percentage of people living below 
the poverty line to 17.98% by the terminal year (2001-02). State-wise

criteria of one US dollar a day.

Protection to Sri Satya Sai Baba 
SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY (K arnataka): Hon. Chairman, 
Sir, this Special Mention is directed towards the Home Ministry, as it 
pertains to the security of Bhagvan Sri Satya Sai Baba who ordinarily 
resides in ashrams situated at Puttaparthi in Andhra Pradesh and 
Whitefield in Karnataka. 
The Deccan Herald newspaper, which is a leading daily in 
Karnataka, has reported that the Swamiji is facing threat from the 
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam. Sir,  the Press report states that the 
Karnataka State police and Andhra Pr adesh police are in the process 
of analysing the threat perception. I would like to state that the Home 
Departments of the two States have to act on the assumption that the 
threat exists and provide the Swamiji all the security prescribed in the 
textbook. Considering the recent attack of the LTTE on the Sri Lankan 
Airport and the growing menace of Naxalites in Andhra Pradesh, it is 
my humble appeal that utmost cauti on be exercised in addressing this 
issue. In the recent past, disrupt ive elements and terrorists were 
focussing on VIP's and are trying to gain mileage and publicity by 
attacking them. 
Sir, Bhagvan Sri Satya Sai Baba is a Divine asset of our 
country and a saint of the highest order and his spirituality is known all 
over the world. His contribution to mankind, by establishing hospitals, 
universities, water supply systems and social philanthropy cannot be 
described in words. Considering the above facts, I request the 
Government to immediately initiate appropriate security measures and 
provide the Bhagvan the highest de gree of proximal and distant 
security cover.

STATEMENT AND DISCUSSION ON RECENT INCIDENTS OF 
KILLINGS IN JAMMU AND KASHMIR 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI L.K. ADVANI): 
Madam, Deputy Chairman, the Members are well aware that terrorist 
groups in Jammu & Kashmir have continuously showed total 
disregard for the yearning for peac e and normalcy on the part of the 
people of Jammu & Kashmir, and did not respond positively to the 
Government's unilateral Ramazan peace initiative. 
Following the withdrawal of Non Initiation of Combat 
operations, the security forces have stepped up oper ations against 
the terrorists.   Significant 
265 

RAJYA SABHA [9 A ugust, 2001] 
success  has  been  achieved  in  these  operations,   with  the  
number  of terrorists killed in June being 217, and in July being 233. 
In an effort to divert this pressure, terrorists have been 
resorting to high visibility acts of violence in Jammu & Kashmir. During 
this period, terrorists have carried out such attacks on innocent 
civilians in J&K attack at Sheshnag Amarnath Yatri Camp on 21s1 July, 
2001, two separate incidents of killing in Doda-Kishtwar area on 21 s' 
and 22nd July, 2001, a third incident in the same general area of Doda-
Kishtwar on 4lh August; and indiscriminate firing on innocent people at 
Jammu Railway Station on the 7lh  of August, 
2001. 
The objectives of the militants in carrying out such attacks 
appear to include : 
- To stretch the Security Forces by forcing them to provide 
- protection in more and more areas thereby hoping to 
blunt -present thrust and momentum of counter-terrorism 
operation in J and K. 
- To create a communal divide with possible repercussions 
not only in J and K but also in the rest of the country. 
- To strike terror among the common citizenry. 
- To force minorities to flee to  safer places thereby giving 
the terrorists space for their activities to be carried out 
freely. 
- To attract media attention both nationally and 
internationally. 
The Government is determined to thwart the nefarious 
designs of the terrorists and their mentors across the border, and not 
to let the counter insurgency grid be thinned out. Nor would we reduce 
the anti-infiltration posture of our  security forces. We remain 
committed to take all possible steps for the protection of remote, 
scattered and minority populations in the State of J and K. 
My colleague, Shri I.D. Swamy along with the Special 
Secretary J&K Affairs in my Minist ry visited Srinagar and Sheshnag 
on 22 nd July, 2001 to assess the securi ty situation in the State and 
held detailed discussions with Hon'ble Governor, J and K and Security 
Forces and the State Government functionaries. Shri Swamy again 
visited Jammu on the 23 rd July, 2001  along with Shri Chamanlal 
Gupta, MOS (Civil Aviation) and a 
266 

[9 August. 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
senior official of MHA, and reviewed security arrangements in the 
Jammu region. Shri I.D. Swamy further visited village Atoli and 
Gopalgarh on the 6 ,h of August, 2001 alongwith Special Secretary 
(JKA) and, thereafter, held a meeting with members of the operation 
groups of the United Headquarters at Jammu. 
Yesterday, a meeting was convened in New Delhi by me to 
have a comprehensive review of the security situation in Jammu and. 
Kashmir including in Doda-Kishtwar region. The meeting was 
attended by the Defence Minister, the Railway Minister, the Governor 
of Jammu and Kashmir, the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, 
alongwith senior officers of the Home and Defence Ministries, State 
Government, the Army, the CPMFs and the Intelligence agencies. 
The State Government has decided to extend the already 
declared Disturbed Areas as per the Armed Forces (Jammu and 
Kashmir) Special Powers Act, 1990 to the remaining portions of 
Jammu province. At present only 20 kilometres belt along the 
International Border/LoC in Jammu province and all districts of 
Kashmir valley stand declared as "distrubed" since 1990. 
The Unified Headquarters have been directed to initiate fresh 
tactics and modified dynamic deployments to ensure that people in 
affected areas, and especially in Do da-Kishtwar, feel reassured and 
confident. 
The number of SPOs authorised for Doda has been increased 
by 1,000 and, along with increasing the effectiveness of existing 
Village Defence Committees, setting up of Dhoke Defence 
Committees for the grazers who go into the remote forest in higher 
reaches will also be experimented with. 
Special intelligence driven security force operations based on 
surprise and speed would also be considered as per requirements of 
the ground situation. 
Measures for upgrading secu rity arrangements at Jammu 
railway station, includi ng its fencing and better illumination as well as 
coordinated security efforts for the station were agreed upon. 
It was also decided that measures as per law against the 
overground supporters of the terrorist s would be stepped up by the J 
and K Police. 
I wish to assure this august House that the Government shall 
leave no  stone   unturned   in   bringing   back  peace   to   Jammu   
and   Kashmir.

and support of all of you who represent the masses of India. It must be 
appreciated that what we are fight ing is a proxy war of multiple 
dimensions unleashed by an inimic al neighbouring country which has 
had no qualms in rationalising the brutal killing of innocent men, 
women and children as "a freedom struggle". 
I seek the support and cooperation of all members of this hon. 
House for the Government's determined bid to crush militancy and 
terrorism in the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

SHRI S. VIDUTHALAI VIRUMBI (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Vice-
Chairman, Sir, through the statement that has been made by the hon. 
Home Minister, the Government seeks the support and cooperation of 
all the Members of this august House. We hope, Sir, even those of our 
colleagues, who have criticised the Government on this issue, will 
stand by the Government as one when the question of unity and 
integrity comes. This message should go across the country to reach 
the people for whom it ought to be. Sir, from the statement we find 
that the Doda-Kishtwa r area was attacked on 21 81 - 22 nd July, 2001, 
i.e., immediately one week after the Agra Summit was held. 
Subsequently, on 23rd July, the Minister of State for Home Affairs went 
to Jammu area, and reviewed the security arrangement. But, after 
this, on 4m August, again the same Doda-Kishtwar area was subjected 
to attack by the militants. Sir, if you look at the dates of the first attack 
and the second attack, it would clearly show that these attacks were 
made only within a period of 12-13 days after the Minister reviewed 
the situation. Sir, it makes us feel  that security arrangements as well 
as the intelligence agencies have to be further strengthened. The 
Sheshnag Amarnath Yatri Camp was attacked on 21 8I July. If we 
remember, last year also, the Amarnath Yatri Camp was attacked by 
the militants. On the 22nd, the Doda-Kishtwar area was attacked. And 
again it was attacked within a gap of 10 days or 15 days. Sir, this time 
also the militants adopted  the same type of stra tegy, which they had 
adopted during the last year. It was repeated again this year. 
Therefore, we feel, Sir that our Intelligence agencies have to go 
through all these things.   When we, the politicians, are able to see 
that

giving me an opportunity to speak on this subject. Mr. Arjun Singh is

SHRI P. G. NARAYANAN (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Vice-Chairman, 
Sir, the situation in Jammu and Kashmir is serious. It has become still 
grave, after the failure of the Agra Summit. The cross-border terrorism 
and infiltration of Pakistani militants into our area is increasing day-by-
day. The activities of the terrorists  have been intensified. After the 
Agra Summit, admittedly, the killi ngs in Jammu and Kashmir have 
gone up. Sir, innocent civilians, including women and children, are 
being killed by the militants. In the month of July, twenty-one civilians 
were brutally killed by the militants. In the month of August, thirteen 
civilians, belonging to the Hindu minority, were killed. During the 
festival day of Rakhi, seventeen peo ple were abducted from a village 
to a jungle and fifteen of them were killed. This tragic incident really 
dampened the festive mood in and around that area. This type of 
barbaric and cruel killings of civilians is highly condemnable by one 
and all. The militants also attacked the Jammu Railway station and 
killed ten civilians, including two women.  This may be due to security 
lapse. 
This clearly shows the Home Ministry's incapability in 
protecting the people of Jammu and Kashmir. We understand that 
Village Defence Committees were formed in some villages to deal 
with this situation. But they were  not provided with adequate facilities. 
Had those committees been provided with better facilities, like arms, 
uniforms, wireless sets, and other basic requirements, they would 
have been able to combat the militancy effectively. So, I request the 
Government to look into this matter. Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, I submit 
that the Central Government and the State Government are 
responsible for the killings of civilians in Jammu and Kashmir because 
the Government is often seen issuing statements that the Government 
is committed to crush the militancy and terrorism. But merely issuing 
statements would not serve the purpose. The Government must come 
forward to deal with the situation with real seriousness. The 
Government must chalk out some strategy for combating this serious 
situation firmly, in order to prevent  this type of killings permanently. 
After the failure of the Agra Summit, Pakistan is threatening to step up 
militancy. I urge upon the Government to take adequate steps to deal 
with this situation. If the Home Ministry is unable to protect the people 
of Jammu Kashmir, then the Home Minister has no right to continue in 
office. So, I demand that the Home Minister, Shri L K. Advani, should 
step down, in the interest of the nation.  Thank you very much.
